title: The starter Nav Bar arranges itself like a real bar
goal: Drag the Nav Bar out of the Library, make it wider, and its back label should stay on the left while its title stays where it belongs, without anyone opening the Layout section. Today it is a box of pieces pinned by hand, so it is the one starter that cannot show off how a bar is actually built.
notes: Found while building the spread gap task on 2026-09-05: its acceptance suggested demoing spread on the starter Nav Bar and it cannot be done. StarterComponents.navBar builds .free(width: 320, height: 48) with a Background (fill), a Divider (horizontal stretch + vertical bottom), a Back label pinned at x=14 and a centred Title. Turning it into a Row stack by hand pulls the Divider into the flow as an item, because isSurface needs stretch on BOTH axes. Options worth weighing: leave it Free and place the pieces with LayerPlacement (cheapest, and already half true), or make the bar a Row stack with the divider kept out of the flow, which needs a way to say "this is chrome, not a row" beyond isSurface. See queue/audits/2026-09-05-spread-gap.json.
acceptance: Dropping the Nav Bar and dragging it wider keeps the back label at the left edge and the title where it belongs, with no typing in the Layout section
The hairline along the bottom still spans the bar and still hugs the bottom, and is not treated as one of the things being arranged
The surface behind the bar still fills it whatever the bar is doing
Picking the dropped Nav Bar and reading the Layout section shows an arrangement a person would recognise as the one they can see

log.note: Adversarial review before building. Reproduced first: the CURRENT Free bar already resizes correctly (back holds the left, title recentres, hairline spans and hugs the bottom), so acceptance 1-3 were not broken. The real gap was acceptance 4 and what the notes said: it cannot be a row, because a row counts the hairline as a fourth control and stands 320 points of nothing in the line. Rejected the cheap option (leave it Free): the Layout section would go on saying Free about something obviously shaped like a bar, and you could never add a second control to it.

Rejected the broad rule 'any rule on the flow's own axis pulls a piece out of the flow'. It would yank pieces out of existing stacks the moment somebody stacked a group with leftover rules on it, which is exactly the case LayerPlacementTests.aStaleRuleOnTheOwnedAxisIsInert exists to protect. Built the narrow one instead: stretching ALONG the way a stack runs steps out, because the flow is what hands out the room along itself, so a row asking for all of it was never a request it could honour. Fill is the way to say 'take what is left over' and keeps its own name.

Landed. ResolvedPlacement.stepsOutOfTheFlow(of:) is the rule; GroupFlow.placed now spans each stepped-out piece per axis instead of only filling the surface; arranged, wrapRooms, PlacementEditing, LayerGeometry and heightIsFilled all read it. StarterComponents.navBar is a Row (gap 12, padding 0/14/0/14, 320x48) with the surface, the hairline and the title all stepping out.

Title is centred on the WHOLE bar, not in the room the back label leaves. A row that put it after the back label would fail StarterComponentRenderTests.aCentredLabelIsActuallyCentred, which has always demanded the bar's title ink be within 2px of the bar's middle. Changing that is a look change the user should make, not the loop.

Found while doing it: centred text sat 2 points right of the middle of its box, because the slack a measurement leaves sits on the far edge and CoreText centred inside the whole stored box. Fixed in TextRasterizer.alignedWidth: centred and right-aligned words lay out in naturalSize's own constraint. Left-aligned text (every label written before alignment existed) is untouched.

Adversarial review of the BUILT thing, on the real app, is what caught the one regression: the title's box is the whole bar, so drawn on top it answered for every click meant for the back label (verified with a playtest, selection came back as Title). Fixed by drawing the title UNDER the controls, re-verified: clicking Back now picks Back, clicking the middle picks Title.

Verified in the probe with Scripts/playtest/nav-bar-row-walk.json (Screen Recording granted, real window captures). All four acceptance items hold: dragged to 640 wide the back label is still 14 in and the title still centred; dragged to 120 tall the hairline came down with the bottom and stayed 1 point; the surface fills; the Layout section reads Stack / Row / Width Fixed 640 / Height Fixed 48 / Gap 12 / Padding 0-14-0-14 with Title, Divider and Background listed as pieces with a rule of their own. Eight related auto-layout walks still run ok. Full suite 3652 tests green.

Filed a-control-dragged-off-the-shelf-onto-an-open-gro: the row lines a second control up in the model, but a tile dragged off the shelf onto an open bar lands beside it rather than in it, so a person cannot try that part yet.
